title: Deep clustering reveals weak tremor three days before the 2021 Geldingadalir eruption
summary: Unsupervised deep clustering of historical seismic recordings revealed a weak tremor beginning around midday on 16 March 2021, roughly three days before the Geldingadalir eruption in Iceland. Harmonic–percussive signal separation on the same recordings supported the timing. The analysis covered one eruption and relied on one seismic station. Prospective eruption forecasting remains untested. The finding was reported in a preprint on 5 May 2023 and published in Communications Earth & Environment on 2 January 2024.
ai_technology: Deep embedded clustering with a convolutional autoencoder
organization: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences; University of Potsdam; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Figure 3 shows the tremor after harmonic–percussive separation. A reanalysis restricted to 12–19 March recovered a similar cluster across several cluster counts, with some misassigned windows. Both checks use the same historical station records.
evidence.unknown: Recurrence across eruptions, discrimination from non-eruptive unrest, and prospective alert performance remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A convolutional autoencoder and deep embedded clustering grouped one-hour seismic spectrograms by learned features. The continuous-tremor cluster directed the authors to check the pre-eruptive interval.

source_review.scope: Full publisher article, including Methods, Results and figure captions; primary preprint Crossref abstract and posting metadata. Figure images and the linked GFZ PDF were not independently inspected.
